claims: The Artemis II mission features the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion capsule.
The Artemis II mission will reach speeds of approximately 24,500 mph (39,430 km/h) to achieve escape velocity for the Moon.
During reentry, the Orion capsule will hit the atmosphere at about 25,000 mph (40,000 km/h) to test the heat shield.
The SLS rocket will push Orion to speeds exceeding 17,000 mph to reach Earth orbit.
Orion will accelerate to over 24,500 mph for the trans-lunar injection.
During the trans-lunar coast, gravity will slow the spacecraft to approximately 3,400 mph during the journey to the Moon.
According to Boeing and USA Today, the Orion capsule will reach 25,000 mph (roughly Mach 33) upon returning to Earth.
As described by BBC and Sky at Night Magazine, parachutes will slow the capsule to approximately 17 mph for a safe landing in the Pacific Ocean.
Artemis II will make a 10-day trip around the Moon.
Artemis II marks the first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit in over 50 years
